nt: Yahweh is using a word that expresses a strong feeling of urgent invitation. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [Hey]

Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [everyone who longs for what I offer, come to me and receive it]

The words **you** and **your** and the implied “you” in the imperatives **listen** and **eat** are plural because Yahweh is addressing the people of Israel. So use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.
לָ֤⁠מָּה תִשְׁקְלוּ־כֶ֨סֶף֙ בְּֽ⁠לוֹא־לֶ֔חֶם וִ⁠יגִיעֲ⁠כֶ֖ם בְּ⁠ל֣וֹא לְ⁠שָׂבְעָ֑ה

Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke the people for spending their resources on what does not truly nourish or satisfy them. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You should not weigh out silver for what is not bread, nor your labor for what does not satisfy!]

Yahweh is speaking of spending effort and money on things that do not satisfy as if it were paying **silver** for something that is **not bread**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [do you pay silver for what cannot sustain you]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **listen** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [Listen very carefully to me]

Here, **your soul** represents the whole person, that is, you yourself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [yourself]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **fatness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [by rich food] or [by abundant food]
